findings.where: Page heading 'Best Hostels in Canggu' (first screen, desktop and phone), and the 'coming soon' notice at the foot of the page
findings.fault: The heading promises a list of the best hostels, but the page has no hostels at all. A visitor only learns there are no listings from the notice at the very bottom, after reading the whole guide. Nothing on the first screen says what MantaHostels is or that this is a guide, not a ranking.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who arrives from a search for 'best hostels Canggu', usually on a phone, expecting names to compare. They scroll to the end, find nothing to choose from, and feel the title was bait. That is bad for a product whose claim is to be the trusted discovery layer.

findings.where: 'Good for' tag group (desktop first screen; phone first slice)
findings.fault: Twelve tags list almost every kind of traveller, including some that pull against each other (Budget, Nightlife, Yoga, Couples, Solo travellers, Long stays). No part of the guide says who Canggu does not suit or names a downside, such as cost, traffic or crowds. So it can't help anyone judge whether the place suits them, and it reads like a tourist board, not honest advice.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker this page is for: they came to judge fit, and a list that says yes to everyone gives them no way to rule Canggu out. A seasoned traveller will read the all-positive tone as marketing and trust the guide less.

findings.where: End of the page: the 'coming soon' notice and the footer
findings.fault: The page ends with nowhere to go. There's no way to hear when Canggu listings arrive, and no link to another destination's guide. The 'Destinations' nav link points to an anchor (#destinations) that doesn't appear anywhere on this page.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who was persuaded by the guide and wants the next step. With no route on, they leave for an OTA and Manta never hears from them again, which is exactly the visitor a pre-launch page needs to keep.

findings.where: 'How we rank' in the nav and in the footer
findings.fault: On a page titled 'Best hostels', the only route to how the ranking works is a link that points back to this same page, which holds no ranking method.
findings.who_objects: A careful traveller who wants to know why a site calls something 'best' before trusting it. The product's own principle says ranking methods are published, and this link promises that method but doesn't deliver it.

findings.where: The guide as a whole and the footer
findings.fault: Nothing on the page shows the guide is current: no 'updated' date and no copyright year. The only sign of who stands behind it is a bare email address in the footer.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning their next stop. Canggu's cafés, surf breaks and hostel scene change fast, so they can't tell whether this advice is from this season or several years old, and they have no named source to trust.

findings.where: The 'coming soon' notice block near the foot of the page
findings.fault: A plain 'listings are coming' message sits in a bright red box, which reads as an error or a warning that something is broken.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor who reads a red panel as a failure. They come away thinking the site is broken rather than early, which undercuts the calm, honest tone the brief asks for.

findings.fault: The heading is in Title Case. The brief's voice asks for sentence case everywhere.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who set sentence case as a binding brand voice rule. A visitor gets a slightly generic, SEO-template feel that is off the brand's relaxed tone.
